contracts.statement: Predicate-evaluation authority belongs to the head that parsed it: a PromQL/LogQL label matcher (CAP-LABEL-MATCHER-EXPRESSION), a LogQL line filter (CAP-LINE-FILTER-EXPRESSION), and a TraceQL scoped span-attribute predicate (CAP-SPAN-ATTRIBUTE-FILTER) each lower to their own chplan.Filter expression and are evaluated per that head's own matching semantics. It pins WHERE-authority (the plan-level chplan.Filter boundary and the optimizer's pushdown/transpose rules never changing a predicate's value), not each predicate kind's own external-spec fidelity — SIGNAL-LABEL-MATCHER-CONSISTENCY, LOGQL-LINE-FILTER-REGEX-SEMANTICS and TRACEQL-SPAN-ATTRIBUTE-TYPE-COERCION own that narrower, kind-specific claim.

The transpose rules' idempotence is proven by internal/optimizer/termination_test.go, shared evidence with ARCH-HEAD-OPTIMIZE-001; no binding here independently re-verifies that a TRANSPOSED Filter's predicate value survives the move for every one of the three predicate kinds — it inherits that proof rather than re-establishing it.

contracts.statement: The shared CH circuit breaker shields every head from amplifying a transient ClickHouse outage into a request storm: it opens after N consecutive failures inside its window, fast-fails while open, probes exactly once during HALF-OPEN even under concurrent callers, and closes again on a successful probe. This state-machine logic is proven deterministically against a fault-injecting fake driver.Conn; the SAME contract is proven again against a REAL ClickHouse outage (a genuine k3d pod-kill) end to end, including the documented 502-then-503 rejection ordering and /readyz reporting circuit in its body while /healthz stays unaffected.
blind_spots: The deterministic evidence exercises the breaker's Client surface directly against a fake driver.Conn; it proves the state machine's own transition logic, never whether a real deployment's actual failure timing (dial latency, TCP RST versus timeout) trips the SAME thresholds the same way.

The live-stack evidence gates the network-partition scenario on a runtime kube-router-enforcement probe: when the pinned k3d image is not actually enforcing NetworkPolicy, that scenario records not-applicable rather than a vacuous pass, and the breaker contract is covered by the pod-kill scenario instead for that run — a single green run does not by itself distinguish a genuinely-not-applicable precondition from one that has permanently stopped materialising; only the separate weekly chaos-not-applicable-rate audit resolves that ambiguity.

Live-stack chaos is informational only (push-to-main + nightly + manual dispatch, never a PR gate, never in release.yml's RELEASE_REQUIRED_CHECKS) — a red run here never blocks a merge or a release, even though a red run is a real failure to fix, never a tolerated one (docs/test-strategy.md's own 'informational does not mean tolerated' framing).

contracts.statement: A handler holding a streaming ClickHouse cursor owns closing it through chclient.CloseCursor before cancelling that query's own context — never the reverse — and that close completes within chclient.CursorDrainBudget regardless of how much of the result set went unread. Closing before cancelling is what lets clickhouse-go release the pooled connection back to the idle pool instead of destroying the socket outright; bounding the drain is what stops a client that walks away mid-stream from pinning a pool slot for as long as ClickHouse takes to finish streaming an abandoned result set.

The deterministic ordering and drain-bound tests (test/regression/cursor_teardown_order_test.go) run against a fake cursor; they prove the HANDLER's own call order and timeout, never whether a real pooled connection is actually returned or destroyed by that order — only conn_teardown_integration_test.go's real-server evidence proves that consequence, and it proves it directly at the chclient API boundary, not through any HTTP seam, so it says nothing about which CALLERS get the order right.

The real-network evidence pins max_block_size so the result streams past the driver's block-buffer depth; with a single block the driver's own teardown branch is a coin flip and the two arms stop diverging (docs/test-strategy.md, Layer 6f) — a future change to that pinned setting could silently make the differential vacuous without failing outright.

contracts.statement: internal/chclient's data-shard fan-out gate bounds how many concurrent ClickHouse dispatches one query may hold open at once, sized once from Config.DataShardCount (or an explicit multiplier override) and shared by every dispatch path — QueryCursor, QueryStrings, QueryOpen — that composes it. DataShardCount<=1, the value of every deployment that predates this field, allocates no semaphore at all; a cancelled dispatch issues KILL QUERY before releasing its slot so the abandoned query actually stops consuming server resources instead of merely freeing local bookkeeping; that release is idempotent; and a gate denial is breaker-neutral, never itself tripping the CH circuit breaker.
blind_spots: Every assertion here runs against a fake driver.Conn; whether a REAL ClickHouse server actually honors the issued KILL QUERY and frees its own resources promptly is unproven — no real-clickhouse-substrate binding exists for this specific claim today (tracked as cerberus issue #3489, filed rather than silently widened into an existing binding's claim).

This is a DIFFERENT fan-out axis from Layer 12's SQL-plan compute fan-out (peak intermediate rows versus leaf scan rows inside one dispatch, ARCH-COMPUTE-FANOUT-CARDINALITY-BOUND-001's own claim): this contract bounds concurrent DISPATCH COUNT to ClickHouse, Layer 12 bounds ROW CARDINALITY inside one dispatch. A deployment can satisfy one while violating the other.

DataShardCount>1 with a custom multiplier is a configuration surface no deployment currently ships in production (cerberus issue #3081/#3128's own 'zero behavior change' framing); the concurrency-cap and multiplier-scaling evidence is exercised only synthetically, never against a real multi-shard ClickHouse cluster.

contracts.statement: Each API head owns its own admission budget, drawn from its own semaphore, wired into that head's own serving surface: HEAD-PROMQL's CERBERUS_ADMIT_PROM, HEAD-LOGQL's CERBERUS_ADMIT_LOKI, and HEAD-TRACEQL's CERBERUS_ADMIT_TEMPO each cap that head's own admit.New(BudgetRequest) semaphore, and HEAD-LOGQL additionally owns a fourth, fully independent budget — CERBERUS_ADMIT_TAIL, admit.NewTail(BudgetTail) — scoped only to the long-lived /tail WebSocket and drawn from a separate semaphore than HEAD-LOGQL's own request budget. Saturating any one of these four budgets rejects only a caller drawing on that budget: it consumes no capacity from, and triggers no rejection against, any of the other three. Rejection surfaces in the shape native to its caller's transport — an HTTP caller gets 503 Service Unavailable with a Retry-After header (admit.Limiter.Middleware), a gRPC stream gets codes.ResourceExhausted (admit.Limiter.StreamInterceptor), and an already-upgraded /tail WebSocket gets a 1013 (Try Again Later) close frame instead of either — and in every case, releasing a held slot returns its capacity regardless of whether the request completed, returned an error, or its handler panicked, so a subsequent caller on that same budget is admitted. records.title: anchoredRegexPattern's anchor wrap is blanked, reopening #1741's stream-selector over-match
records.notes: Blanks anchoredRegexPattern's anchorPrefix/anchorSuffix constants (internal/chsql/builder.go:847-848) from "^(?:" / ")$" to "", reopening issue #1741: job=~"ap" (or, here, LogQL's env=~"prod|stg" stream selector) would again match "production" as a substring instead of rejecting it, since ClickHouse's match() is a substring search and Prometheus/Loki/Tempo regex matchers are always fully anchored. Scoped to the label-matcher path deliberately: anchoredRegexPattern is called only from chplan.OpMatch/OpNotMatch sites (internal/chsql/builder.go's exprBinary and exprNestedArrayExists) — LogQL line filters (`|~`/`!~` against the log line) lower to a distinct chplan.LineContent node in internal/logql/lower.go's lineFilterPart and never call this function, so their already-unanchored (Loki-correct) substring semantics are untouched by this mutation, preserving the stream-selector/line-filter distinction the grounding issue calls out. THIS MUTATION IS NOT LOGQL-ONLY: anchoredRegexPattern is the one SQL-emission site chplan.OpMatch/OpNotMatch shares across PromQL, LogQL and TraceQL (see LOGQL-LABEL-MATCHER-REGEX-ANCHORING's and PROMQL-LABEL-MATCHER-REGEX-ANCHORING's own blind_spots, and the cross-head SIGNAL-LABEL-MATCHER-CONSISTENCY contract) — the primary detector is the LogQL fixture (test/spec/logql/stream_regex_no_overmatch.txtar, the regression fixture #1741 itself added), and the second detector is PromQL's own regression twin (test/spec/promql/regex_unanchored_no_overmatch.txtar) included as SUPPLEMENTARY, disclosed evidence of the same shared-emitter blast radius rather than a second independent bug — both are expected to report killed for the identical root cause, not two uncorrelated findings. Both detectors share test/spec's generic spec.Walk/spec.Match golden-comparison harness (structural sql/args/chplan text diffing) — that harness is head-agnostic plumbing, not part of either head's own independent evidence; what differs per detector is the head-specific Lower() entry point and its own fixture corpus. Neither detector needs the chdb build tag or a live ClickHouse: the kill is a static sql/args/chplan text mismatch against the golden, verified before chDB round-trip execution is even reached (see internal/logql/lower_test.go's TestLower and internal/promql/lower_test.go's TestLower, both gated on no build tag). records.title: lowerPipelineWithLabels walks MultiStages back-to-front, breaking label-extraction-then-filter order
records.notes: lowerPipelineWithLabels (internal/logql/lower.go, lowerPipelineWithLabels's own MultiStages loop) walks a pipeline's stages strictly left-to-right in source order per LOGQL-PIPELINE-STAGE-ORDER, threading the growing `labelsExpr` forward so a stage occurring AFTER a label-extracting parser stage (`| json`, `| logfmt`, `| regexp`, `| unpack`) sees its extracted keys, while a stage occurring BEFORE it does not. This mutation reverses the iteration (`for i := len(e.MultiStages) - 1; i >= 0; i--`) so every pipeline's stages are visited back-to-front instead. Query used by the detector: `{job="api"} | logfmt | status > 400` (test/spec/logql/filter_numeric.txtar) — under CORRECT left-to-right order, `| logfmt` runs first and merges the extracted `status` key into labelsExpr, so `| status > 400` resolves it and correctly keeps only the two rows with status 500/503. Under the REVERSED mutant, `| status > 400` is lowered FIRST against the still-bare ResourceAttributes/LogAttributes columns (status is not a real column in either), so its presence probe is unconditionally false and the whole predicate degenerates to drop every row — a genuinely different, observably wrong result using actual supported LogQL syntax, not an invented shape. This is the label-mutation/filter-order case the grounding issue calls for: a query+dataset pair where swapping stage order changes labels/results, not merely the shape of an already-order-independent predicate. Two existing fixtures are already bound to the LOGQL-PIPELINE-STAGE-ORDER contract (BINDING-LOGQL-PIPELINE-STAGE-ORDER-FILTER-THEN-LINE over edge_label_filter_and_then_line_filter.txtar, and BINDING-LOGQL-PIPELINE-STAGE-ORDER-UNPACK-FORMAT over edge_multistage_filter_unpack_format.txtar) but neither actually depends on stage order: both compose two SQL predicate-only stages (or a predicate stage plus a post-fetch-only `| unpack`/`| line_format` pair with no SQL impact), so their ANDed predicates are order-commutative and verified NOT to change under this exact reversal mutation (checked by hand before selecting filter_numeric.txtar instead) — this is precisely the coverage gap LOGQL-PIPELINE-STAGE-ORDER's own blind_spots entry already names ("this contract's ordering claim rests entirely on the fixed TXTAR fixture set"), so filter_numeric.txtar's kill is new, real evidence for the labels-threading half of the contract, not a restatement of the two existing bindings. This mutation is scoped to internal/logql/lower.go (LogQL's own package-local pipeline loop) and does not touch internal/chsql/builder.go or any other head's lowering, so there is no shared-emitter/PromQL/TraceQL side effect to report here (unlike MUTANT-LOGQL-LABEL-MATCHER-UNANCHORED-1741's anchoredRegexPattern mutation). The detector needs no chdb build tag or live ClickHouse: the kill is a static sql/args/chplan text mismatch against test/spec/logql/filter_numeric.txtar's golden, reached before any chDB round-trip execution (internal/logql/lower_test.go's TestLower, no build tag). test/property/logql_test.go + test/property/oracle/logql/evaluator.go (this issue's other cited grounding) were evaluated as an alternative/additional detector and deliberately NOT used: the property/oracle shape roster (test/property/gen/shapes.go's logQLShapeRoster, referenced by LOGQL-STREAM-PIPELINE-PROPERTY-COVERAGE's own blind_spots) draws at most one pipeline stage per generated query and never composes a parser stage with a dependent label filter, so it cannot exercise this bug class at all today — adding that coverage is out of this change's scope (no wholesale local-oracle rewrite, no arbitrary stage permutations) and, if wanted, belongs in a separate filed issue rather than folded into this mutant record.

records.title: chsql.CounterDelta's reset-detection comparison is neutered so it never fires
records.notes: Real production seam, not a textual stand-in: chsql.CounterDelta (internal/chsql/builder.go, the typed compound-idiom behind counterDeltaFrag in internal/chsql/range_window.go ~2690-2707) renders `arrayMap((p, c) -> if(c < p, c, c - p), ...)` -- the counter-reset-aware pairwise delta rate()/increase() reduce over. The patch changes the comparison's second operand from `p` to `c` (`Lt(BareIdent("c"), BareIdent("p"))` -> `Lt(BareIdent("c"), BareIdent("c"))`), which is always false, so the emitted SQL always takes the `c - p` branch and the reset-compensation arm never fires: this is a disable, not merely an inversion. gen.CounterResetCase (test/property/gen/counter_reset.go) seeds a genuine mid-window reset (20 -> 5 between adjacent samples, not a duplicate timestamp -- see that file's header on why test/property/rate_dup_timestamp_test.go's duplicate-timestamp dataset does not exercise this). Locally reproduced end to end: the unmutated code returns the Prometheus-correct increase() = 33.333... (100/3); with this patch applied to a scratch copy the same query returns 6.666... (20/3, i.e. last-first with no reset added back), and TestPromQL_CounterResetMidWindowCompensation fails with exactly that drift. TestPromQL_RangeWindowBoundaryExactSample (the sibling MUTANT-PROMQL-RANGE-WINDOW-BOUNDARY-CLOSED-LEFT's own detector) was re-run against this same patch and still passes, confirming the two mutants are independently attributable.

records.title: emitRangeWindowOverTimeDirectInstant's window-start predicate becomes closed-left
records.notes: Real production seam: emitRangeWindowOverTimeDirectInstant (internal/chsql/range_window.go ~3378-3412) is the row-level WHERE that answers an instant count_over_time()/min_over_time()/max_over_time()/present_over_time() query -- the incrementally-reducible *_over_time family internal/chsql/range_window.go's emitRangeWindowOverTimeDirect routes to a direct CH aggregate rather than the groupArray+arrayFilter windowed-array path. records.notes:

Both detectors seed the SAME bounded branching-tree fixture #3444/#3518 added to gen/traceql.go (root -> childA -> grandchild, root -> childB) so the depth-two case is a real, wire-observed discriminator rather than an assumed one: the direct-child query `{root} > {grandchild}` must return zero matches and the descendant query `{root} >> {grandchild}` must return exactly one, on both the HTTP /api/search transport (test/property/traceql_test.go, real parse->lower->optimize->emit->chDB->HTTP pipeline) and the gRPC streaming Search RPC (internal/api/tempo/grpc, real *grpc.Server over bufconn against the same chDB session) independently. Both were hand-verified to fail (kill) against this exact patch and to pass cleanly against the unmutated tree before this record was added.

Limits: the branching-tree fixture is a single FIXED topology (branching factor 2, max depth 2 — traceQLBranchingTreeSpanCount in gen/traceql.go) and only chdb-backed local pipelines are exercised here — no live reference-Tempo differential (compatibility/tempo/driver) carries an equivalent grandchild-depth structural case today; its seeder fixture is a flat root+children shape with no third generation, so `>` and `>>` never diverge there. records.title: lowerAttribute swaps the resource/span attribute carrier columns
records.notes:
lowerAttribute (internal/traceql/lower.go) resolves a scoped attribute reference to its carrier column; this patch swaps the two branches so `resource.<key>` reads SpanAttributes and `span.<key>` reads ResourceAttributes. Both detectors target TraceQLScopeCollisionAttributeKey (`environment`, #3444/#3518's gen/traceql.go), the same key stamped into BOTH maps per span with disjoint value pools so a scope mix-up cannot coincidentally pass.

The HTTP detector runs the traceql.selector.scope-collision-conjunction shape from the property roster (`{ resource.environment = X && span.environment = Y }`) through property.CompareTraceIdentityOutcomes, the TraceID-multiset comparator this repo's TRACEQL-PROPERTY-EVIDENCE-TRACE-IDENTITY contract documents — reused as-is, not reimplemented.

The gRPC detector (internal/api/tempo/grpc) is a genuine equal-cardinality, wrong-identity case, not a count difference: it seeds two traces whose resource/span environment values are exact MIRRORS of each other (trace1: resource=prod/span=shadow; trace2: resource=shadow/span=prod), so the swapped query matches exactly one trace either way — just the WRONG one (trace2 instead of trace1) under the mutation. A bare match-count assertion is blind to this; the detector asserts the exact matched TraceID instead, which is what catches the misattribution.

Both detectors were hand-verified to fail (kill) against this exact patch — the HTTP shape roster reports two missing traces (empty result where two were expected); the gRPC case reports the wrong TraceID — and to pass cleanly against the unmutated tree.

Limits: TraceQLScopeCollisionResourceValuePool / TraceQLScopeCollisionSpanValuePool are each only 2 values wide, and no live reference-Tempo differential (compatibility/tempo/driver) carries an equivalent same-key resource/span collision case today. See issue #3528 for a related, separately-filed contracts.json documentation gap this same generator strengthening exposed.
